answer: Three established identities cross-sign a new one, and the signature carries liability: if the recruit farms, 20 percent of each signer's escrow burns with it, and each signer may recruit 50 per year. That caps one compromised identity at 50 downstream accounts. A free design lets one operator field 10,000 entries at no marginal cost. Here the 10,001st identity costs three escrow losses. A plume of burned collateral stays in the ledger, the violet flag stays beside the signer, and the prism of one operator splitting into many accounts gets expensive at the same rate it gets wide.
